sentence_items.revised_english: Egypt is Sudan's most important northern neighbour and a party to the Nile regime. The 8 Nov 1959 Cairo agreement allowed Egypt to build the Sudd el-Aali (High Dam) at Aswan and Sudan the Roseires reservoir (UNTS6519_1959). From 1 Feb 1958 Egypt claimed the territory north of the 22nd parallel, opening the Halaib dispute (IBS18_1962) [CONTESTED]; effective Egyptian control dates are contested – 1992/93, 1994, 1995 or 2000 depending on source (see db/halaib_dates_check.md; WP_HALAIB). Under Nimeiri, Sudan backed Egypt after the 1979 peace with Israel; Mubarak gave Nimeiri asylum in 1985, and after 1989 relations collapsed: Egypt hosted the opposition NDA, accused Khartoum of aiming Iraqi missiles at the High Dam, and by mid-1991 openly funded the DUP and SPLM (LOC1991_EGYPT; LOC1991_FOREIGN). Egypt has always opposed the GERD; Sudan, after first backing it under Bashir, hardened its stance after the Oct 2021 coup as the two armies held joint exercises (GEO-015). In the 2023 war, Egypt and Saudi Arabia back the Sudanese army (ICG_ETH_ERI, 'A Seesaw Relationship'); see also GEO-012 (Egyptian state-affiliated, pro-SAF) and AR_AJCS_5653.
